t: A stock policy issued for 8 months at an annual premium equivalent of ₹25,000 is cancelled by the insured after 2 months. The premium retained is
e: For short-period policies, premium is retained at the applicable short-period scale for the time in force: 2 months = 30% of annual rate = 30% × ₹25,000 = ₹7,500.

t: When a fire policy is cancelled at the option of the insurer, refund of premium is
o: On pro-rata basis for the unexpired term
e: AIFT Rule 10.2: at the insurer's option refund is pro-rata for the unexpired term; at the insured's option retention is on the short-period scale.

t: Which of the following is excluded from the STFI group of perils under SFSP?
o: Flood resulting from earthquake or volcanic eruption
e: STFI covers storm, cyclone, typhoon, tempest, hurricane, tornado, flood and inundation, excluding those resulting from earthquake, volcanic eruption or other convulsions of nature (deleted when the EQ add-on is taken).

t: A factory's bulk oil storage tank bursts inward due to a sudden vacuum created while emptying it. This is
o: Covered only under the Leakage add-on
e: Implosion is bursting inward/collapse due to external pressure and is covered along with explosion; exclusions are own explosion of steam boilers (other than domestic) and centrifugal forces.

t: An SFSP policy on a factory with sum insured ₹60 crore at the location suffers a fire loss of ₹30 lakh. The compulsory excess is
e: SI above ₹10 crore up to ₹100 crore per location: 5% of the claim subject to a minimum of ₹25,000; 5% of ₹30 lakh = ₹1,50,000, which exceeds the minimum.

t: Which of the following does NOT cause the SFSP insurance to cease to attach?
o: Passing of interest in the property by will or operation of law
Alteration of the trade carried on, increasing the risk, without sanction
Sale of the property to a third party without endorsement
Unoccupancy of the building for more than 30 days
e: Condition 3: cover ceases on alteration of trade increasing risk, unoccupancy beyond 30 days or transfer of interest except by will or operation of law, unless the insurer's sanction is endorsed.

t: Under Condition 13 of the SFSP policy, if the parties cannot agree on a sole arbitrator within 30 days, the dispute is referred to
o: A panel of three arbitrators, one appointed by each party and the third by the two arbitrators
e: Arbitration under the Arbitration and Conciliation Act 1996: sole arbitrator by agreement, failing which within 30 days a panel of three; obtaining the award is a condition precedent to any suit.

t: Within how many days of a loss must the insured deliver a written claim with particulars under Condition 6 of the SFSP policy?
e: ★ Key fact (repeated across the mocks of this paper). Condition 6(i): notice of loss forthwith, and within 15 days (or such further time as the insurer allows in writing) a written claim with particulars and details of other insurances.

t: Every notice or communication to the insurer under the SFSP conditions must be
o: Made in person at the issuing office
e: Condition 14: every notice and other communication required by the conditions must be written or printed.

t: Under an RIV policy, until the insured has actually incurred expenditure on reinstatement, the insurer is liable
o: For 50% of the reinstatement cost as advance
Only up to the amount that would have been payable without the reinstatement memorandum (market value)
e: RIV special provision: no payment in excess of the amount payable without the memorandum until expenditure has been incurred by the insured on replacement or reinstatement.

t: Spoilage Material Damage cover for machinery, containers and equipment in specified blocks is rated at
e: Spoilage cover: stocks in specified blocks 5 × policy rate; machinery, containers and equipment 2.5 × policy rate; subject to average on the specified blocks.

t: The Insurance of Additional Expenses of Rent for Alternative Accommodation can be granted to
o: Godowns for the period of reconstruction
Non-manufacturing premises only, for a maximum indemnity period of 3 years
Any industrial risk for up to 12 months
e: Conditions: non-manufacturing risks; under the fire policy not CL policy; max indemnity 3 years; non-kutcha buildings; same city; tenant or owner-occupant; owner-occupant must insure building and contents.

t: An owner-occupant takes alternative accommodation at ₹40,000 per month while his damaged office (standard rent fixed by the municipal authority ₹25,000) is rebuilt. The additional rent recoverable per month is
e: For an owner-occupant, additional rent = rent of alternative accommodation − standard rent based on rateable value fixed by municipal/revenue authority = 40,000 − 25,000 = ₹15,000.

t: A declaration policy (SI ₹2 crore) last declared stock of ₹1 crore, whereas the stock that ought to have been declared was ₹1.5 crore. A loss of ₹30 lakh occurs with value at risk ₹1.5 crore. The claim payable is
e: Average is applied twice: first by the last declaration ratio 30 × 1/1.5 = ₹20 lakh; the SI/VAR ratio (2/1.5) exceeds 1, so no further reduction.

t: Under a declaration policy, the reinstatement premium collected after a claim is
o: Distinct from and not taken into account in the final adjustment of premium
Adjusted against the next monthly declaration
Added to the declarations for refund calculation
Refunded at the end of the year
e: Declaration Clause condition 5: extra premium on the loss amount pro-rata to expiry is not taken into account in the final adjustment; the notes also state RI premium is not considered for declaration refund.

t: Which statement about the Escalation Clause is correct?
o: It applies to all fire policies on buildings and machinery, not only to reinstatement value policies
It applies to stocks as well
It applies only to reinstatement value policies
It operates only on the renewal date
e: AIFT Rule 12(e): escalation applies to all policies, not restricted to RIV; (d) it applies to building, machinery and accessories, not stock; the increase operates daily from inception to the date of loss.

t: A factory block protected by hand appliances, a hydrant system and an independent sprinkler installation with an AMC in force is eligible for an FEA discount of
e: FEA discounts: hand appliances + trailer pumps/fire engines 2.5%; + hydrant 5%; + sprinkler/water spray 7.5%; hand appliances + hydrant + sprinkler 10%. Discounts are not cumulative and need TAC/LPA certification and an AMC.

t: A factory rateable under Section IV stops all manufacturing and storage activity continuously for 45 days. The premium retention for the silent period is
o: The appropriate storage rate or the silent risk rate of ₹1.00‰, whichever is higher
Nil, as the risk is silent
e: AIFT Rule 19: silent risk = no manufacturing/storage for 30 days or more; retention at storage rate or ₹1.00‰ whichever is higher; silent rates not allowed after a loss and no discounts apply.

t: Which of the following perils is covered under Bharat Griha Raksha but is only an add-on under SFSP?
e: BGR perils = SFSP 12 + impact by insured's own vehicles, forest fire, spontaneous combustion + EQ, terrorism and theft within 7 days (12 + 3 + 3).

t: A 24-month EAR policy with total premium ₹19 lakh is to be paid in instalments. The number of instalments and the first instalment are
e: ★ Key fact (repeated across the mocks of this paper). n = (T − 6)/3 + 1 = (24 − 6)/3 + 1 = 7. First instalment = 0.05P + 0.95P/n = 95,000 + 18,05,000/7 = 95,000 + 2,57,857 = ₹3,52,857; other instalments ₹2,57,857 each.

t: Under Bharat Griha Raksha, long-term policies are permitted up to
o: 10 years, with escalation of 5% per year on the inception sum insured
e: BGR allows long-term policies up to 10 years with automatic escalation of 5% per year; inbuilt covers include loss of rent, alternative accommodation rent, 5% professional fees and 2% debris removal.

t: Property A: PML ₹10 crore on SI ₹100 crore; Property B: PML ₹15 crore on SI ₹50 crore. Which is the better risk?
o: Property A, as its PML is lower both absolutely and as a proportion of SI
Property B, as its PML is higher
Property B, as its SI is lower
e: A risk with a lower PML is considered better; higher PML leads to higher rates and larger facultative needs.

t: A manufacturer's finished goods valued at ₹1 crore per the latest sale invoice are destroyed by fire; the gross profit margin is 15%. The amount payable under the fire policy is
e: Profit is not payable under a material damage policy; finished goods are valued at invoice value less gross profit: 100 − 15 = ₹85 lakh.

t: An LOP policy has an accumulated stocks clause. Reduction in turnover from the fire was initially made good by selling finished stock worth ₹10 crore; a further ₹15 crore reduction appeared next year after stocks were depleted. The rate of GP is applied to
e: Accumulated stocks clause: equitable allowance is made where the shortage in turnover is postponed by maintaining turnover from accumulated finished stock, so the stock consumed (₹10 crore) is treated as reduction in turnover.

t: Which policy should be recommended for the construction of a dam where civil works dominate?
e: CAR covers civil engineering projects such as dwellings, factories, dams and roads; where civil work exceeds 50% of project value, CAR rather than EAR is issued.

t: A CAR policy issued for a road project has expired before completion. Extension of the period is
o: Possible for the remaining value plus 50% of the completed portion
Possible only for the full original sum insured
Possible for the balance sum insured excluding the completed portion not yet put into service
e: Extensions of project policies are granted for the uncompleted portion; the completed and handed-over portion drops out of cover.

t: Under an EAR policy with the escalation extension, under-insurance would apply only if
o: The escalation premium is paid in instalments
The cost of replacement of the affected item exceeds its original value plus the escalation amount
The project is delayed beyond the policy period
Any increase in replacement cost occurs
e: With escalation opted, settlement is on the original site value plus increase in replacement cost up to the escalation percentage; average applies only beyond that.

t: A 3-year-old wire rope of a crane is replaced in an MBD claim at a cost of ₹2,00,000. The amount payable before excess is
e: ★ Key fact (repeated across the mocks of this paper). Ropes in lifts, cranes and ropeways attract depreciation of 15% per year subject to a maximum of 75%: 3 × 15% = 45%, so 2,00,000 × 55% = ₹1,10,000.

t: Where premium is refundable at final adjustment of an EAR policy, refund against the escalation premium collected is
o: Not allowed, though additional escalation premium is charged where additional premium is due
e: Premium adjustment on completion does not cover prime cost or escalation premium; additional escalation premium is charged on an upward adjustment but no refund is allowed on a downward one.

t: For an AOG claim (earthquake) under a CAR policy, the excess is
o: 5% of the claim with a minimum of ₹10,000
20% of the claim with a cap of ₹3 crore
10% of the claim amount subject to a minimum of the testing period excess, with an upper limit of ₹5 crore
e: Major perils/AOG (EQ, STFI, landslide, subsidence, lightning): 10% of claim, minimum testing period excess, upper limit ₹5 crore.

t: Under EAR/SCE, the excess is applied on the net claim amount after adjusting
e: Excess is deducted last, after depreciation, salvage and under-insurance have been applied to the assessed loss.

t: Debris removal under an EAR/CAR policy is
o: An inbuilt cover up to 1% of the claim
An additional cover available for extra premium, limited to debris of insured property
e: Clearance and removal of debris is an extension; debris of uninsured property is not an add-on available under the project policy.

t: Which of the following cannot be covered as 'surrounding property' under EAR/SCE/CAR?
o: Existing plant and machinery of the principal
Existing storage tanks adjacent to the works
e: Owner's surrounding property covers existing property of the principal at or adjacent to the site; construction/erection machinery is insured under CPM.

t: The qualifying examination for an individual insurance agent conducted by the Insurance Institute of India is:
e: ★ Core fact (asked across III papers). IC-38 is the agents' pre-recruitment examination; IC-01/02/11/14 are Licentiate papers.

t: Second-hand machinery is being erected under an EAR policy. Which statement is incorrect?
o: The policy can be issued for projects with second-hand machinery
Dismantling cover can be granted for additional premium
Appropriate deduction is made on claims for second-hand machinery
Testing cover for second-hand machinery is automatically included
e: For second-hand machinery, dismantling can be covered at extra premium and claims attract appropriate deductions; integrated testing cover is not automatic.

t: Under the instalment facility for project policies, the first instalment is
o: 5% of the total premium plus an equal share of the remaining 95%
e: I1 = 0.05P + 0.95P/n; the remaining instalments are 0.95P/n each; the minimum interval is 3 months and the last instalment falls 6 months before expiry.

t: Which pair of wordings is equivalent in scope?
e: DE5 and LEG3 both give full cover for defective and non-defective property once damage occurs, excluding only improvement costs; DE1 ≈ LEG1; DE4 ≈ LEG2.

t: Under EAR/CAR, the cost of alterations, additions or improvements made while repairing damaged items is
o: Covered if approved by the surveyor
Covered up to 10% of the repair cost
e: Settlement is limited to restoring items to their pre-loss condition; betterment, alterations and improvements are excluded.

t: A project owner wishes to insure the loss of anticipated gross profit from delay in commissioning caused by an insured erection accident. The appropriate policy is
e: ALOP indemnifies the principal for actual financial loss from delayed commencement of commercial operations due to damage admissible under the CAR/EAR policy.

t: Under MBD, when repairs are carried out in the insured's own workshop, the insurer pays
o: The quotation of an outside repairer
Nothing, as own-workshop repairs are not admissible
Cost of materials and wages incurred plus a reasonable percentage for overhead charges
e: MBD basis of indemnity for own-workshop repairs: materials, wages for the repair and a reasonable percentage to cover overheads.

t: A spare rotor kept for a turbine is insured under MBD. The discount applicable to the spare is
e: Discount for spares such as rotors of generators, compressors, turbines or windings of transformers is 50%; stand-by machines also get 50% (except DG sets).

t: The MBD policy becomes void unless its continuance is agreed by endorsement in the event of
o: A change in the number of shifts only
Material change in the original risk, alteration or addition to the insured item, or change in the insured's interest
e: Material change in risk, alteration/modification/addition to the insured item and change of the insured's interest all require the insurer's endorsement.

t: In EEI, the term 'computer equipment' covers the entire system comprising
o: CPU, keyboard, monitor, printers, stabilisers, UPS and system software
e: The whole computer system including peripherals, stabilisers, UPS and pre-loaded system software is the insured 'equipment' under EEI.

t: Which of the following is NOT a definition under the BPP policy?
o: 'Explosion' means sudden violent rending of the boiler structure by internal pressure with forcible ejection of contents
'Chemical explosion' means an explosion arising out of chemical reaction in any plant
'Flue gas explosion' means explosion of ignited gases in the furnaces or flues
'Breakdown' means sudden mechanical or electrical failure of the boiler
e: BPP covers explosion and collapse of the insured boiler (plus optional surrounding property and TPL); breakdown is not a defined or covered event – that falls under MBD.

t: Contractor's plant and machinery worth ₹10 lakh, used on an EAR-insured project, may be covered under the EAR policy itself as a CPM extension provided the value
e: Per the question bank, CPM can be covered under EAR/CAR as an extension where the CPM value does not exceed ₹25 lakh; larger values need a separate CPM policy.

t: Which of the following is an exclusion under a Deterioration of Stocks policy?
o: Escape of refrigerant following damage to the plant
Collapse of the rack structure in the cold chamber
Rise in temperature from compressor breakdown
Breakdown of stand-by DG sets where FOES is opted
e: DOS excludes fire/AOG, building collapse, war/RSMD, consequential loss and rack collapse (not a machinery breakdown risk); stoppage under 24 hours and temperatures not exceeding 4.4°C are also excluded.

t: A corporate agent may tie up with a maximum of how many insurers in each line of business?
e: ★ Core fact (asked across III papers). Raised from 3 to 9 insurers per category (life, general, health) by the 2022 amendment to the Corporate Agents Regulations.

t: Before a claim can be admitted under an MLOP policy,
o: A claim must be admissible under the underlying MI or BPP material damage policy
A claim must be paid under the fire policy
The machine must be declared a total loss
The indemnity period must have fully expired
e: Material damage proviso: MLOP responds only when the loss is admissible under the machinery insurance/BPP policy.

t: Under the deductibles circular, an IAR policy is available to industrial risks (including petrochemical) with overall sum insured of at least
o: ₹100 crore in one or more locations in India
₹10 crore in one or more locations
e: The circular makes industrial risks with overall SI of ₹100 crore and above (one or more locations) eligible for IAR; the trainers note that eligibility is now ₹50 crore under products filed with IRDAI.

t: The minimum deductible for Boiler insurance under the circular is
o: 1% of the sum insured subject to a minimum of ₹2,500
5% of the claim amount subject to a minimum of ₹10,000
e: Boiler insurance: 5% of claim, minimum ₹10,000; MBD: 1% of SI per machine, minimum ₹2,500; EEI: as per TAC tariff.
